comparison: Perfect agreement on anatomical validation (C25-C30). Both evaluations find the tract-tracing and immunofluorescence data convincingly support selective targeting of D1- and D2-SPNs. Reviewers explicitly praised the anatomical validation approach.

Perfect agreement on electrophysiological validation (C31-C35). Both evaluations confirm the optogenetic efficacy is well-demonstrated with appropriate controls. Reviewers explicitly validated the electrophysiology data and specificity of targeting.

Perfect agreement on methodological rigor (C82-C112). Both evaluations affirm the behavioral procedures are well-documented, appropriately controlled, and sufficient for replication. Reviewers praised the systematic and rigorous approach with sophisticated behavioral assays.
Perfect agreement on D2 receptor signaling rationale (C45). Both evaluations accept this explanation for why prior pharmacological approaches were less decisive than the current optogenetic method.

Strong agreement on D1-SPN necessity for PIT (C36-C39). Both evaluations support these findings with OpenEval noting C36-C39 plus specificity controls (C55-C57), while peer review groups C36-C39 with C55-C57 and C3 together. Both praise the specificity controls showing preserved value-based choice.

Strong agreement on behavioral specificity (C55-C57). OpenEval evaluates these claims separately as supporting selective PIT impairment, while peer review groups them with D1-SPN behavioral findings (C36-C39). Both emphasize the importance of preserved magazine entries and outcome devaluation performance.

Strong agreement on D2-SPN necessity for PIT (C41-C44). Both evaluations strongly support this novel finding. OpenEval addresses C41-C44, while peer review includes C53 (both D1 and D2 necessary). Both note this is the first direct demonstration using optogenetics, addressing limitations of prior pharmacological studies.

Strong agreement on D1-SPN→VP circuit role (C46-C49). Both evaluations support terminal-specific silencing data showing D1-SPNs mediate PIT via VP projections. Peer review additionally includes C4 and C54 (differential VP involvement), while OpenEval addresses C54 separately with uncertainty.

Agreement on uncertainty regarding D2-SPN→VP null results (C50-C52). Both evaluations express concern about interpreting negative results without validation of terminal silencing efficacy. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to lack of validation; peer review similarly notes the null result 'leaves open the possibility' of incomplete manipulation. Peer review includes C5.

Agreement on theoretical model integration (C66, C76-C79). Both evaluations support the mechanistic interpretation, though OpenEval expresses uncertainty about C66 (D2-SPNs acting locally) due to unvalidated D2→VP terminal silencing. Peer review endorses the 'nuanced interpretation' of local D2-SPN regulation without expressing uncertainty.

Agreement on theoretical model description (C68-C75). Both evaluations accept the theoretical framework from prior work as appropriate contextualization. OpenEval notes the model is well-cited but not directly tested; peer review views it as thoughtful discussion that adds to the literature. Peer review additionally includes C6 and C79.

Agreement on background literature (C1-C15). Both evaluations support these claims establishing PIT and NAc-S context. OpenEval explicitly validates the literature representation; peer review implicitly accepts by affirming the study appropriately builds on prior work. Peer review additionally covers C16-C24 in this evaluation.

Agreement on methodological limitations of prior work (C17-C22). Both evaluations support these claims about pharmacological and molecular approach limitations. OpenEval addresses these separately; peer review groups them with broader background claims (C1-C24), affirming the study resolves conflicts in the literature.

Agreement on NAc-S→VP literature (C23-C24, C60-C64). Both evaluations support these anatomical and functional claims from prior literature. OpenEval groups C23-C24 with C60-C64; peer review covers C60-C65 plus additional claims (C40, C58-C59) as accepted background knowledge.

Agreement on translational implications (C80-C81). Both evaluations support these speculative discussion points about clinical relevance. OpenEval notes appropriate speculation; peer review endorses as thoughtful discussion of implications. Peer review additionally includes C67.

Agreement on future directions (C67). Both evaluations support this as appropriate speculation about D1-SPN projections to lateral hypothalamus. OpenEval addresses separately as reasonable future work; peer review groups with translational implications as thoughtful discussion of limitations and future research.

Partial overlap on differential SPN contributions (C53). OpenEval groups C53 with C54 and rates as UNCERTAIN due to unvalidated D2→VP terminal silencing. Peer review groups C53 with C41-C44 and rates as SUPPORTED, strongly endorsing that both D1 and D2-SPNs are necessary for PIT.

Partial overlap on differential VP involvement (C54). OpenEval rates C53-C54 as UNCERTAIN due to lack of D2→VP validation. Peer review groups C54 with D1→VP findings (C46-C49, C4) and rates as SUPPORTED, noting 'selective involvement of D1 but not D2 neurons in this circuit.'

Agreement on A2a-Cre rationale (C59). Both evaluations support this claim about A2a receptor expression in D2-SPNs. OpenEval addresses separately with citation; peer review groups with broader literature-based claims as accepted background.

Agreement on D2-SPN projection patterns (C65). Both evaluations support this anatomical claim about VP vs lateral hypothalamus projections. OpenEval addresses separately with citations; peer review groups with broader anatomical literature as accepted background.

Minimal overlap on prior PIT literature (C40). OpenEval groups C40 with D1-SPN behavioral findings (C36-C39) as supporting context. Peer review includes C40 in broader literature review (C40, C58-C65) as accepted background knowledge.

Minimal overlap on NAc-S→VP background (C23-C24). OpenEval groups C23-C24 with C60-C64 as VP-related literature. Peer review includes C23-C24 in comprehensive background evaluation (C1-C24) affirming the study builds appropriately on prior work.

Minimal overlap on model claims (C79). OpenEval groups C79 with C66, C76-C78 as theoretical model integration rated UNCERTAIN. Peer review groups C79 with C68-C75, C6 as theoretical framework rated SUPPORTED as appropriate contextualization.
